long_biography.plain_text:
Years in his father's dredging company gave Howard 'Boone' Kenyon a practical education in moving earth and water. In 1978 he set out on his own, initially building small subdivisions around Baton Rouge. When high interest rates weakened that market, he redirected the young company toward water and sewer installation in Morgan City.

Following the work brought B&K Construction into New Orleans and then into concrete and flood-control projects. From 1995, its crews specialised in lining drainage canals, eventually completing more canal bottoms in the regional SELA programme than any other contractor. The business expanded into pile driving, levees, structural concrete, deep excavations and large-diameter utility work. Projects completed during Kenyon's lifetime included the South Claiborne covered canal, Florida Avenue canal widening and two water towers built for New Orleans' water-hammer mitigation programme.
